evidence.declaration_text:
Run one pixel-art command on a drawing or image you already made. This is
the engine's own command line: it checks work, explains it and improves it.

Commands: check and explain (read-only):
- lint <id> [--rules outline_gap,orphan_pixel,…] — pixel-art defects, each
  naming the node and command that drew them
- inspect <id> --region x0,y0,x1,y1 --scale 10 — a zoomed crop with its
  exact colours
- measure <id> --at x,y — what is at a pixel and who drew it
- explain <id> — resolved geometry, per-command footprints, before rendering
- motion / storyboard / silhouette / reveal / clusters / parts <id> — reports
- score <id> — a 0-100 pixel-art discipline score with a breakdown
- compare <id> <id> — two results side by side
Improve (returns a NEW drawing id):
- shade <id> --band 2 --light=-1,-1 — banded shading along a colour ramp
- selout <id> — selective outlining; reoutline / clean-lines / aa / mirror
- cluster <id> --at x,y --action recolor --color <name> — one guarded cluster
- repair <id> — deterministic cleanup of drift, strays, fringe and noise
Sheets and frames (returns a NEW image id):
- split <image> --grid 3x3 — a sprite sheet, strip or grid as an animation,
  one frame per cell (columns x rows)
- join <image> <image> … [--as sheet|rows|animation] [--columns n] — pictures
  or animations as one sprite sheet, one per row, or one animation
- scale <image> --by 4 — the same picture or animation bigger, each pixel a
  4x4 block (a sticker, a print); nothing is redrawn
A result comes back as an image in the reply AND as a no-auth URL the reply
prints, `/mcp/pixel-tools/<id>/image.png` (`frames.png` for the frames of a
multi-frame one) — so a sheet you joined is both readable inline and
downloadable. Sheets hold at most 1024 px a side; `join` refuses a larger
one rather than shrinking the art, and says how many frames do fit.
Craft operations need colour ramps: run `extract-palette <id>` first, then
pass `--ramps skin=dark,mid,light`.
Authoring: `edit <id> --changes '[…]'` applies exact pixel operations and
`draw <id> --recipe '{…}'` builds or revises a layered scene; both take JSON
whose fields are NOT listed here. Colours in that JSON are always `#RRGGBB`
or `#RRGGBBAA` with alpha `00` or `ff` — `rgb()` and bare hex are refused,
and nothing strips the `#`, since argv is a JSON list rather than a shell
line. Every `edit` change carries `operation`, `layer`, `frames` (ONE-based)
and `reason`; coordinates are zero-based and a `region` is `[x0,y0,x1,y1]`
inclusive. Then its own fields: `patch_pixels` takes `pixels`, a list of
`[x,y,expected,replacement]` (1-10000, each assigned only where the pixel
already holds `expected`, so a mismatch fails the pass); `copy_region` takes
`source_layer`, `source_frame`, `region`, `at` `[x,y]`; `map_colors` takes
`region` and `colors` `{"#from":"#to"}` (alpha must match); `flood_fill`
`seed`/`expected`/`color`; `brush` `points` plus `color`; `outline` `mode`
(outside|inside|recolor|erase). The full contracts and any command's flags
are one free call away: `describe edits | paint | outline | draw | animation
| motion | scenes | review`, `<command> -h`, `describe cli`.
Free for subscribers.

PixelLab AI-powered pixel art generation service.

Use of this service is subject to PixelLab's Terms of Service:
https://pixellab.ai/termsofservice

This MCP server provides programmatic access to generate:
- Characters with multiple directional views
- Character animations
- Isometric tiles
- Top-down tilesets for game maps
- Sidescroller tilesets for platformer games

All generation operations are non-blocking and return job IDs for status tracking.
Requires PixelLab subscription (with credit fallback support).

**Pixel tools (free, exact, you are the artist)**: one command line, pixelart_workbench(argv=[...]), inspects, edits, draws and animates pixel art by your own decisions; combine it with the AI tools above. Start with pixelart_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start'], mode='low'|'high') — low acts directly with few tokens, high plans out loud and reviews every frame. Animated effects (spells, hits, explosions, auras): vfx_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start']) — same ids, exports to the user's My effects.

**Git access**: Clone and push game project source code with standard git.
Use `list_projects` to see your projects and their git clone URLs.

exec tool declaration:
```ts
declare const tools: { mcp__pixellab__pixelart_workbench(args: {
  // One command line, e.g. 'lint <drawing_id> --rules outline_gap' or ['edit', '<id>', '--changes', '[…]']. Omit it for the playbook. A subject is an id or an image reference — never a file path; the server writes the output and returns a new id. A reference is `character:<id>:<direction>` for a rotation, `character:<id>:<direction>:<animation>` for every frame of that animation (the display name, type or [group: ...] id get_character prints), the same two forms for `object:<id>` (a one-direction object's direction is the literal `unknown`), `gallery:<id>`, `job:<id>`, `upload:<id>`, a data URL, an https link or base64. That is how a stored animation's pixels come back inline without downloading anything. Start with 'describe cli' for the full command list.
  argv?: string | Array<string> | null;
  // low (default): act directly, fewest tokens — one decisive image per result. high: think openly — fuller evidence and a review checklist; write your plan and observations in `notes`. Use the mode the user asked for.
  mode?: "low" | "high";
  // What you observed and what this step should achieve, in a few sentences (high mode: always; low: optional). On the first call, include the user's request. Stored with the step to improve these tools.
  notes?: string | null;
}): Promise<CallToolResult>; };
```
evidence.schema_representation: JSON Schema projection of the exposed TypeScript argument declaration: argv string | string[] | null, mode 'low' | 'high', notes string | null; additionalProperties false
evidence.subject_transport: Each argv subject is a data:image/png;base64 URL of the exact retained seed bytes (declaration: a subject is an id or an image reference, including a data URL, an https link or base64; never a file path). Base64 computed from the artifact file and verified to round-trip to the same sha256.
